sentences.text: Paratomistoma is an extinct genus containing only one species, classified as a gavialoid crocodylian.
Despite being unfused, the holotype skull is considered to represent a morphologically mature individual.
Named in 2000 by paleontologists Christopher Brochu and Philip Gingerich, the type species P. courti honors Nicholas Court, who discovered the holotype specimen.
Researchers suggest that Paratomistoma may have lived in marine or coastal environments.
Recent molecular studies indicate that Tomistominae, including Paratomistoma, belong to the family Gavialidae rather than being crocodiles, placing the genus within the parent group Tomistominae.
Paratomistoma lived during the Bartonian stage of the Middle Eocene, between 41.03 and 37.71 million years ago.
